source_review.notes: Checked current official NASA guidance for Technical Requirements Definition, good-requirement writing, Requirements Management, Logical Decomposition, verification matrices, Stakeholder Expectations and Configuration Management; active NASA-HDBK-1009A; final OMG SysML 2.0; and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018. Nine final URLs returned HTTP 200 through direct command-line retrieval. ISO returned HTTP 403 to scripted curl but its official current standard record was independently retrieved through browser access on the review date. Claims are bounded to semantic requirements objects, rationale/assumptions, bidirectional typed relationships, validation, verification planning and controlled baselines.

evidence: Reviewed the requirement tuple, typed graph, decomposition-adequacy implication, independent requirement/verification state spaces, typed trace matrix, coverage indicator and budget composition expression.
Confirmed identifiers, normative fields, applicability, sources, rationale, assumptions, status and version remain distinct from relationships and evidence.
Confirmed coverage and conjunction expressions are explicitly limited to declared scope and exposed assumptions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The formal notation structures requirements reasoning but does not turn a graph edge into logical proof or compliance evidence.

evidence: Executed requirements-model-integrity-check and reproduced five requirements, five unique IDs, four parent edges, zero orphan parents and zero derivation cycles.
Recomputed five single-normative-statement records, five quantified field sets, five rationales, five allocations, five verification links and zero unresolved placeholders.
Confirmed the original checker attempt correctly failed because Python attempted to sum truthy unit strings; the predicate was corrected to return explicit booleans before review completion.
Confirmed the corrected declared model produces requirements_model_consistent with exact stdout.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The counts describe five declared teaching objects only; they do not establish parent-child sufficiency, value correctness, feasibility, satisfaction or verification.

evidence: Confirmed child conjunction plus explicit assumptions is presented as a reviewed adequacy obligation rather than inferred from graph topology.
Confirmed requirement lifecycle state and verification state are modeled independently, preventing approved from implying implemented or passed.
Confirmed trace coverage is a ratio over declared source objects and only indicates presence of permitted relationships.
Confirmed quantitative composition may be additive, worst-case, probabilistic or nonlinear and therefore requires an explicit function, assumptions and uncertainty.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Derivation, decomposition, allocation, satisfaction, verification, conflict and supersession retain different semantics throughout.

evidence: Challenged compound shall statements, absent subjects/conditions/units/tolerances, vague qualities, hidden rationale/design, unjustified thresholds, assumptions disguised as obligations and unmanaged TBD/TBR values.

Reviewed copied flowdown, circular/orphan parents, insufficient/overlapping children, crosscutting obligations, shared allocations, prospective satisfaction, wrong-configuration verification and passed tests against invalid requirements.

Reviewed incompatible units/reference conditions, duplicate/equivalent text, variant leakage, copied reuse, supplier ownership, conflicting sources, last-edit resolution and stricter-is-safer reasoning.

Reviewed lint false positives, 100-percent wrong trace coverage, stale generated views, baseline mutation, complaint-driven threshold changes and operational evidence that can indict requirement, implementation, test or context.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for configured applicability, authorized source, adequacy reasoning, allocation, evidence, change impact, historical preservation and outcome feedback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real requirements sets still need applicable stakeholder, domain, design, integration, operations, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, legal, regulatory, supplier, verification, validation and authority review.

evidence: Traced stable identity, one normative obligation, subject/action/property, conditions, measures, tolerances, units, applicability, source and rationale through capture and baseline control.
Confirmed needs, assumptions, operational statements, requirements, design descriptions, rationale, procedures and results remain separate object classes.
Confirmed typed acyclic parent relationships require reasons and sufficiency arguments rather than link counts.
Confirmed allocation, satisfaction and verification stay separate, with configured verification cases and empirical evidence.
Confirmed conflicts, placeholders, status dimensions, variants, changes, views, automation and prior baselines remain explicitly governed.
invariant_checking.notes: Structural integrity is treated as necessary but insufficient for the correctness and completeness of the modeled problem.

proof_review.notes: The adequacy implication is a proof obligation template; the chapter presents no completed theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed complete, correct, necessary, sufficient, feasible, consistent, verified, validated, satisfied, compliant, traced and baselined language for evidence and authority scope.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-052/report.json records exact local execution evidence for five declared objects and structural relationships only.
The chapter requires article/configuration, environment, inputs, measures, uncertainty, criteria, evidence and closure authority for verification claims.
A clean graph, generated specification, allocated element, satisfaction link or passed test is never presented as universal system compliance.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. The checker explicitly cannot establish necessity, sufficiency, feasible values or actual product satisfaction.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked requirement, requirements model, normative statement, stakeholder/technical requirement, requirement pattern, applicability, source, rationale, derivation, decomposition, allocation, satisfaction, verification, bidirectional traceability and baseline. Typed relations and normative-versus-informative content remain consistently separated.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked semantic fields, requirement classes, sources/rationale, assumptions/TBRs, derivation/decomposition adequacy, crosscutting ownership, allocation/satisfaction, verification cases, validation, conflicts/duplicates, variants, statuses, change impact, generated views, automation, set review and operational reconciliation. Cases cover conjunctions, latency budgets, availability, units, security, variants, TBRs, redundancy, change and accessibility outcomes.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from requirement-object semantics through typed flowdown, architecture/V&V integration, control and outcome learning. Ten examples and five complete solutions require learners to elicit without fabricated precision, repair a misleading graph, construct a common-cause-aware recovery argument, manage variants and govern a late contracted threshold change.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, requirements-engineering, systems-modeling, stakeholder, domain, architecture, integration, operations, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, legal, regulatory, supplier, verification, validation, configuration-management, or technical-authority review is claimed.
